source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.text: 3. Wickedness cannot give permanent prosperity. root . . . not be moved --firm as a flourishing tree-- ( Ps 1:3; 15:5; Jer 17:8 ).

entries.heading: 4. A virtuous woman
entries.text: 4. A virtuous woman --in the wide sense of well-disposed to all moral duties ( Pr 31:10 ). maketh ashamed --that is, by misconduct. rottenness --an incurable evil.

entries.heading: 5. thoughts
entries.text: 5. thoughts --or, "purposes." are right --literally, "are judgment," that is, true decisions. counsels --(Compare Pr 11:14 ). deceit --contrary to truth and honesty.

entries.heading: 6. The words
entries.text: 6. The words --or, "expressed designs" of the wicked are for evil purposes. the mouth --or, "words" of the righteous delivering instead of ensnaring men.
7. Such conduct brings a proper return, by the destruction of the wicked and well-being of the righteous and his family.

entries.heading: 8. despised
entries.text: 8. despised --as opposed to commended ( Pr 11:12 ). perverse heart --or, "wicked principles," as opposed to one of wisdom.

entries.heading: 9. despised
entries.text: 9. despised --held in little repute, obscure ( 1Sa 18:23; Isa 3:5 ). hath a servant --implying some means of honest living. honoureth himself --is self-conceited.

entries.heading: 10. regardeth
entries.text: 10. regardeth --literally, "knoweth" ( Ps 1:6 ). mercies . . . cruel --as acts of compassion ungraciously rendered to the needy. The righteous more regards a beast than the wicked a man.
11. The idler's fate is the result of indolence and want of principle ( Pr 6:32; 7:7 ).

entries.heading: 12. the wicked . . . evil
entries.text: 12. the wicked . . . evil --They love the crafty arts of deception. the root . . . fruit --their own resources supply them; or, it may be rendered: "He (God) giveth, or, sets ( Eze 17:22 ) the root of the righteous," and hence it is firm: or, the verb is impersonal; "As to the root . . . it is firm" ( Pr 17:19 ).

entries.heading: 13, 14. The wicked is snared,
entries.text: 13, 14. The wicked is snared, &c.--The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.

entries.heading: 15. The way . . . eyes
entries.text: 15. The way . . . eyes --The fool is self-conceited (compare Pr 12:1; 1:32; 10:17; Jas 3:17 ).

entries.heading: 16. prudent . . . shame
entries.text: 16. prudent . . . shame --He is slow to denounce his insulters ( Jas 1:19 ).

entries.heading: 18. speaketh
entries.text: 18. speaketh --literally, "speaketh hastily," or indiscreetly ( Ps 106:33 ), as an angry man retorts harsh and provoking invectives. tongue . . . health --by soothing and gentle language.
19. Words of truth are consistent, and stand all tests, while lies are soon discovered and exposed.

entries.heading: 20. that imagine
entries.text: 20. that imagine --or, "plan" ( Pr 3:29 ). They design a deceitful course, to which, with all its evils and dangers to others and themselves, the happiness of peace-makers is opposed (compare Mt 5:9; Ro 12:18 ).

entries.heading: 21. no evil
entries.text: 21. no evil --(as in Ps 91:10 ), under God's wise limitations ( Ro 8:28 ). mischief --as penal evil.

entries.heading: 22. deal truly
entries.text: 22. deal truly --or, "faithfully," that is, according to promises (compare Joh 3:21 ).

entries.heading: 23. concealeth
entries.text: 23. concealeth --by his modesty ( Pr 10:14; 11:13 ). heart . . . proclaimeth --as his lips speak his thoughts (compare Ec 10:3 ).

entries.heading: 24. slothful
entries.text: 24. slothful --(Compare Margin ), so called because he fails to meet his promises. under tribute --not denoting legal taxes, but the obligation of dependence.

entries.heading: 25. a good word
entries.text: 25. a good word --one of comfort.

entries.heading: 26. more excellent
entries.text: 26. more excellent --(Compare Margin ); or, "more successful," while the wicked fail; or, we may read it: "The righteous guides his friend, but," &c., that is, The ability of the righteous to aid others is contrasted with the ruin to which the way of the wicked leads themselves.

27. (Compare Pr 12:24 ). took in hunting --or, "his venison." He does not improve his advantages. the substance . . . precious --or, "the wealth of a man of honor is being diligent," or "diligence." precious --literally, "honor" ( Ec 10:1 ).
28. (Compare Pr 8:8, 20 , &c.). A sentiment often stated; here first affirmatively, then negatively.
